R001.text: H003 gives n>0 and I has n elements. We prove the two string formulas by induction. At m=0, h v=λv and xv=0 by H005. For the step temporarily assume L1: h y^m v=(λ-2m)y^m v, and, if m≥1, x y^m v=m(λ-m+1)y^{m-1}v (with xy^0v=0 at m=0). From [h,y]=-2y and [x,y]=h in H004, h y^{m+1}v=y h y^m v-2y^{m+1}v=(λ-2m-2)y^{m+1}v, while x y^{m+1}v=y x y^m v+h y^m v=[m(λ-m+1)+λ-2m]y^m v=(m+1)(λ-m)y^m v. This also holds at m=0 using xv=0. Discharge L1; induction proves the asserted formulas for all nonnegative m.

For every i∈I, iteration of F001 gives x^i y^i v=i! λ(λ-1)⋯(λ-i+1)v. For i=0 this is v with empty product 1. For 1≤i≤λ each factor is a positive integer and hence nonzero in ℂ. H005 gives v≠0, so y^iv and e_i are nonzero. Their h-eigenvalues λ-2i are pairwise distinct in ℂ. To check independence, fix arbitrary c:I→ℂ and j∈I, and temporarily assume L2: ∑_{i∈I}c_i e_i=0. Apply ∏_{k∈I,k≠j}(h-(λ-2k)Id). Every term except the j-th is zero; the remaining term is c_j∏_{k≠j}2(k-j)e_j=0. The product and e_j are nonzero, so c_j=0. Since j was arbitrary every coefficient is zero. Discharging L2 and quantifying over c proves that the whole family is linearly independent.

Apply M003 with A=ℂ, T=V, Q=I and f=e. F001 makes I finite and nonempty; F002 supplies independence; H004 and card(I)=n=λ+1 give the required dimension equality. Thus e spans V, so together with independence it is a basis. F001 at m=λ+1 says y^{λ+1}v, if nonzero, is an eigenvector of eigenvalue -λ-2. Expand this vector in the e-basis. Applying h-(-λ-2)Id shows each coefficient times (λ-2i+λ+2)=2(λ+1-i) is zero; these eigenvalue-difference factors are nonzero scalars for i∈I. Hence every coordinate is zero and y^{λ+1}v=0. All higher powers vanish by further application of y.

Divide the string identities F001 by i!: e_0=v, xe_0=0, xe_i=(λ-i+1)e_{i-1} for 1≤i≤λ, he_i=(λ-2i)e_i; directly ye_i=(i+1)e_{i+1} for i<λ, and ye_λ=0 by F003. For r≤i, iteration and division by r! give X_r e_i=[(λ-i+1)⋯(λ-i+r)/r!]e_{i-r}=binom(λ-i+r,r)e_{i-r}; if r>i the iteration passes xe_0=0. Similarly Y_r e_i=[(i+1)⋯(i+r)/r!]e_{i+r}=binom(i+r,r)e_{i+r} when i+r≤λ, and otherwise is zero by F003. These binomial numbers are integers (they count r-element subsets of a set of the indicated nonnegative size). This proves the basis, termination and all the asserted action formulas.

R002.text: By H006 choose an integer basis of M that is also a complex basis of V. Its index set is finite because V has finite complex dimension (H004). M002 applied to this complex basis over ℂ counts its elements as dim_ℂ V=n. N001 gives card(I)=n, so reindexing gives an integer basis indexed by I. This proves F001. H001 ensures R is a subring: products of integers not divisible by the prime p are again not divisible by p, and addition and multiplication of the stated fractions preserve the denominator condition.

Choose f as in F001. M001 with A=ℤ, B=R and T=M gives the R-basis (1⊗f_i)_{i∈I} of M_R. Under ι_R these vectors go to f_i. If ∑ r_i f_i=0 with r_i∈R, complex independence of f gives every r_i=0. Hence ι_R is injective. Its image contains f and therefore spans V over ℂ. This also proves that M_R is free of rank n. From now on identify M_R with this image.

Admissibility H006 makes every X_r,Y_r preserve M; their complex linearity then preserves the R-span M_R. In particular x=X_1 and y=Y_1 preserve M, and h=[x,y]=xy-yx does too by H004. These integral operators obey the Chevalley brackets on M and therefore induce the stated action after tensoring. For any 0≤t≤λ, H003 gives t<p; applying M006 with ℓ=p to this arbitrary t and H001 gives p coprime to t!, hence p does not divide t!. Thus 1/t!∈R and t! is a unit. In particular λ!, j!, (λ-j)! are units for j∈I. The integer identity binom(λ,j)j!(λ-j)!=λ! shows that binom(λ,j) is a unit of R, with inverse j!(λ-j)!/λ!.

Compute on the complex e-basis of N001. X_λ kills all e_k with k<λ and sends e_λ to e_0 with coefficient binom(λ,λ)=1; Y_λ sends e_0 to e_λ with coefficient 1. Thus Y_λ X_λ=E_{λλ}. Also X_{λ-i}e_λ=e_i with coefficient 1, so X_{λ-i}E_{λλ}=E_{iλ}. For E_{λλ}Y_{λ-j}, an input e_k with k<j is sent below e_λ and killed by the projection; if k>j it is sent beyond the end of the string and is zero. On e_j the coefficient is binom(λ,λ-j)=binom(λ,j). Thus E_{λλ}Y_{λ-j}=binom(λ,j)E_{λj}. Composing gives E_ij=binom(λ,j)^{-1}X_{λ-i}Y_λ X_λ Y_{λ-j}. Every factor preserves M_R by F003, and its scalar lies in R. Hence all E_ij preserve M_R. These identities and preservation statements require no distinction of weights modulo p.

R003.text: Use the embedding of N002. E_ii maps M_R onto Jcoord_i e_i, because it extracts the i-th coordinate on the N001 basis. For i,j∈I and c∈Jcoord_j, E_ij(c e_j)=c e_i belongs to M_R by N002, so c∈Jcoord_i. Interchanging i,j proves equality. N001 gives 0∈I and e_0=v, hence the common module is J. The projection E_00 of a finite R-basis of M_R (N002) gives finitely many generators of J e_0; since e_0≠0, their coefficients generate J. Temporarily assume L1: J={0}. Then every projection E_ii would vanish on M_R, and their sum is Id_V, so M_R would be zero. This contradicts its complex span V and n>0 from N001. Discharge L1 to conclude J≠{0}. Finally, coordinate projections show each element of M_R has coordinates in J; conversely each sum ∑ c_i e_i with c_i∈J belongs to M_R. Uniqueness is complex independence of e. Thus M_R=⊕_{i∈I}J e_i.

Put T=ℚ⊗_R J. The multiplication map μ:T→ℂ is defined on simple tensors by μ(q⊗c)=qc. It is well-defined by additivity and R-balancing. Every tensor is a finite sum of simple tensors. Write its finitely many rational first factors over a common nonzero integer denominator d; balancing integer numerators into J writes the tensor as (1/d)⊗c for one c∈J. If its image in ℂ is zero, c/d=0, so c=0 and the tensor is zero. Thus μ is injective. If c_1,…,c_s is a finite R-generating family of J from F001, then 1⊗c_1,…,1⊗c_s spans T over ℚ by tensor bilinearity. In particular T is finitely generated as a ℚ-module, that is finite dimensional.

The coordinate isomorphism in F001 induces an explicit ℚ-linear equivalence Φ:ℚ⊗_R M_R→∏_{i∈I}T: on q⊗∑c_i e_i it gives (q⊗c_i)_{i∈I}. For clarity, define its inverse by summing the maps T→ℚ⊗_R M_R induced by c↦c e_i: a tuple (q_i⊗c_i)_i maps to ∑_i q_i⊗(c_i e_i), extended additively in each entry. Both maps are defined by balanced bilinear maps. On simple tensors their composites are identities, by uniqueness of the coordinates and finite distributivity; simple tensors generate, so these checks prove both inverse identities. This supplies the rationalized direct-sum identification, not just a count.

Put r=dim_ℚ T. N002 supplies an R-basis of M_R indexed by I. Applying M001 with A=R and B=ℚ to this basis gives a ℚ-basis of ℚ⊗_R M_R indexed by I; M002 over ℚ therefore gives its dimension as card(I)=n, using N001. Apply M007 with A=ℚ to T to obtain freeness. The finite generation in F002 and this freeness verify the module premises of M004. Thus M004 with the constant family T over I gives dim_ℚ(∏_{i∈I}T)=∑_{i∈I}r=nr. M005 applied to Φ from F003 equates these dimensions: n=nr. Because n>0, r=1.

Fix arbitrary a,z∈J and temporarily assume L2: a≠0. Injectivity of μ in F002 gives 1⊗a≠0, since its image is a. The singleton family consisting of 1⊗a is linearly independent over ℚ: a scalar annihilating a nonzero vector in a vector space over a field is zero. Apply M003 with A=ℚ, ambient space T, the singleton index type and this singleton family. F004 gives the required dimension 1, so 1⊗z=q(1⊗a) for some q∈ℚ. Applying μ proves z=qa for that q. Discharge L2 and quantify over a,z: for every nonzero a∈J every element of J is a rational multiple of a. Together with F001–F004 this proves the stated coordinate decomposition, injectivity, and rational rank-one conclusion.

R004.text: N003 says J is nonzero and finitely generated. Remove all zero members of a finite generating family. The remaining family still generates, and cannot be empty because J≠0. This proves F001, which will allow the finite minimum construction.

Choose a≠0 in J and a family g as in F001. By the rational-line conclusion of N003, every g_j is q_j a for some q_j∈ℚ; because g_j and a are nonzero, q_j≠0. For a nonzero rational q=A/B with nonzero integers A,B, repeatedly remove factors p from A and B. This process terminates since p≥2 by H001 and absolute values strictly decrease at each removal. Thus A=p^s A', B=p^t B' with s,t≥0 and p dividing neither A' nor B'. Consequently q=p^{s-t}(A'/B'), where A'/B' is a unit of R: both A'/B' and its inverse B'/A' satisfy the denominator condition. Apply this to all the finitely many nonzero rational coefficients of g relative to a. For each there is an integer exponent and a unit of R; the nonempty finite list of exponents has a minimum and an index attaining it. These are precisely the existential data in F002.

Choose simultaneously from F002 the exponent family νexp (entries ν_j), the unit family u, the minimum ν and an attaining index j_0. Put b=p^ν a=u_{j_0}^{-1}g_{j_0}. This is a nonzero element of J, since p^ν is a nonzero rational and a≠0. Every generator g_j equals p^{ν_j-ν}u_j b with ν_j-ν≥0, so g_j∈Rb; conversely b∈J gives Rb⊂J. Therefore J=Rb. Substituting into the unique-coordinate decomposition of N003 proves that every element of M_R is a unique R-linear combination of b e_i: if ∑r_i b e_i=0, N003 gives r_i b=0 for each i, hence r_i=0 since b≠0. Thus these vectors are an R-basis indexed by I, of cardinality n>0. The same argument applies to any nonzero b∈J with J=Rb, proving the full principal-generator and basis assertion.

R005.text: For every integer d not divisible by p its image in K is nonzero, because H002 says the kernel of ℤ→K is pℤ. Thus define ρ(a/d)=bar(a)/bar(d). Equality of fractions is preserved by cross-multiplication, so this is well-defined and preserves sums and products; it extends ℤ→K. The characteristic also factors the integer map through ℱ_p=ℤ/pℤ; primality H001 makes this a field, and its map into K is injective since a unital map from a field has zero kernel. On elementary tensors define A:M⊗_ℤK→M_R⊗_R K by A(m⊗c)=(1⊗m)⊗c. Its inverse sends (r⊗m)⊗c to m⊗ρ(r)c. The balancing relations in the two tensor products verify well-definedness; the inverse identities follow on the displayed generators, since (r⊗m)⊗c=(1⊗m)⊗ρ(r)c. These generators span, so A is a K-linear isomorphism.

The kernel of ρ is pR: for a/d∈R, its image is zero exactly when p divides a, equivalently a/d belongs to pR. Its image is the prime field ℱ_p, because a/d reduces to the quotient of two prime-field elements. Thus R/pR≃ℱ_p. The map M_R⊗_R K→(M_R/pM_R)⊗_{ℱ_p}K sends u⊗c to [u]⊗c. Conversely define [u]⊗c↦u⊗c. A different lift u+pw gives the same tensor since (pw)⊗c=w⊗pc=0. Balancing over ℱ_p is valid: lift a prime-field scalar to r∈R and use (ru)⊗c=u⊗ρ(r)c; changing its lift by pR has no effect. These formulas define inverse K-linear maps on the simple tensors. This proves the second isomorphism as well as its compatibility with the first one.

Choose b as in N004 and define β_i=A^{-1}((b e_i)⊗1). M001 with A=R, B=K and basis (b e_i) gives the K-basis 1⊗b e_i of K⊗_R M_R; the tensor flip sends it to (b e_i)⊗1 in M_R⊗_R K. The flip is an isomorphism because u⊗c↦c⊗u and its reverse are balanced and their composites fix all simple tensors. Transporting along A^{-1} therefore shows that β is a K-basis of V(K). M002 over K counts it: dim_K V(K)=card(I)=n>0 by N001. Also the quotient M_R/pM_R has the basis [b e_i] over R/pR: coordinates in the R-basis of N004 reduce independently, since a combination lies in pM_R exactly when every coefficient lies in pR. Thus β is precisely the reduced basis extended from ℱ_p to K as in the supplied proof.

N001 gives all action formulas on e_i; complex linearity gives the identical formulas on b e_i. N002 says all these operators preserve both M and M_R, and gives the induced Chevalley action after tensoring. In particular the induced x,y,h satisfy [h,x]=2x, [h,y]=-2y and [x,y]=h on V(K), because tensor extension preserves sums and compositions of lattice endomorphisms. The maps A and B above commute with every induced lattice operator: check this on m⊗c and u⊗c using their defining formulas. Therefore the x,y,h formulas on β and the X_r,Y_r formulas are exactly those of N001 with each integer coefficient replaced by its image in K. Explicitly xβ_0=0, xβ_i=bar(λ-i+1)β_{i-1}, yβ_i=bar(i+1)β_{i+1} until yβ_λ=0, and hβ_i=bar(λ-2i)β_i; X_r and Y_r have respectively coefficients bar(binom(λ-i+r,r)) and bar(binom(i+r,r)) in their stated ranges and zero outside. For 0≤r≤λ, N002 makes r! a unit in R, so its image is nonzero in the field K. The integer-operator identities r!X_r=x^r and r!Y_r=y^r hold on M and persist after tensoring. Thus X_r=bar(r!)^{-1}x^r and Y_r=bar(r!)^{-1}y^r.

N002 expresses E_ij=binom(λ,j)^{-1}X_{λ-i}Y_λ X_λ Y_{λ-j} with the scalar a unit in R. Since E_ij(b e_k) is b e_i for k=j and zero otherwise, tensoring this identity yields the coordinate matrix unit T_ij on β with formula T_ij=bar(binom(λ,j))^{-1}X_{λ-i}Y_λ X_λ Y_{λ-j}. Its scalar is nonzero after reduction, since a unit maps to a unit. For an arbitrary K-subspace W temporarily assume L1: W is invariant under x,y. It is then invariant under their nonnegative powers, their scalar multiples, and their compositions. Every divided power appearing in this formula has index between 0 and λ, so F004 shows that it preserves W. Consequently every T_ij preserves W. Discharge L1 and quantify over W. This proves the tensor identifications, reduced basis and formulas, and the matrix-unit invariance assertion.

R006.text: H001 supplies the prime condition for the localized ring occurring in the input N005. N005 supplies β, a K-basis of V(K), of cardinality n>0. H003 gives 0∈I. Its member β_0 is nonzero since basis vectors are independent; hence V(K)≠0. Let W be arbitrary and temporarily assume L1: W is invariant under x,y,h. In particular it is invariant under x,y, and N005 therefore says it is invariant under every coordinate matrix unit on β. If W={0}, the required alternative already holds. For the other case temporarily assume L2: W≠{0}. There is a nonzero vector in W. Its expansion in β has a nonzero coordinate, since an expansion with all coordinates zero would be zero.

Choose w,c,j from F001 within the nonzero branch. For every i∈I, applying the coordinate matrix unit T_ij gives T_ij w=c_j β_i∈W, since it kills all other basis coordinates and preserves W. Because c_j≠0 in the field K and W is K-linear, β_i=c_j^{-1}(c_j β_i) belongs to W. Thus every basis vector belongs to W, so its span, all of V(K), is contained in W. The reverse containment is part of W being a subspace of V(K). Hence W=V(K) in the nonzero case. Discharge L2; together with the zero case this proves W={0} or W=V(K) under L1. Discharge L1 into the antecedent to obtain F002.

Universal introduction over W proves the subspace assertion from F002, and F003 proves V(K)≠0. H004 gives the Chevalley bracket relations and hence closure of the integer span in D014. The action is the induced L(K)-action described in N005 and D014; invariance under its generators x,y,h is exactly invariance under their K-linear span, so this is irreducibility as an L(K)-module. No algebraic closure of K was used. At λ=0 the index set has one element and all relevant factorials and binomial coefficients are 1; all displayed arguments remain valid. At p=2 the allowed λ are 0 and 1 by H003; nothing used distinct reduced h-eigenvalues. These included endpoints satisfy the same conclusion.

1: # Shared-lemma extraction as a local NL0 revision
2: 
3: ## Scope and position
4: 
5: Apply this procedure at the start of **NL0-to-Lean translation**, before final
6: interface/planning freeze or worker-packet generation. It is not an extra
7: requirement for a task that requests NL0 alone. The input is an existing,
8: versioned NL0, not an invitation to reconstruct its proof.
9: 
10: The operation is proof factoring: move an already supplied local derivation
11: into one shared N/R pair and replace its occurrences by explicit applications.
12: Do not rewrite the whole NL0, regenerate its prose, reprove unchanged results,
13: or seek a stronger/general theorem for speculative future reuse. Reading the
14: existing graph to locate candidates is not a new proof-construction task.
15: If an existing N already exports the needed fact, reuse that node directly.
16: 
17: Use [the revision record](../templates/source-refactoring.md). Preserve the
18: original package and audit as immutable evidence. Write a revised package in
19: a new directory; retain existing IDs and keep the revision identity in the
20: sidecar record. Generated Markdown/diagrams are views, never patch authorities.

22: ## 1. Locate and qualify candidates without reconstructing NL0
23: 
24: Start with existing node statements, direct inputs, definitions and any
25: available index. Locate repeated subarguments using their mathematical role,
26: objects, formulas or operation names; then inspect the actual candidate spans
27: and the local context they need. Do not commission a new proof or a full prose
28: summary for every node as a discovery method. Text similarity is only a lead.

30: For each proposed lemma record:
31: 
32: - The complete mathematical statement, all parameters/conditions and proposed
33:   direct input IDs, together with exact old graph pointers or paragraph spans.
34: - The existing derivation to reuse and every occurrence that will consume it.
35:   The derivation must actually supply the proposed statement; a summary label
36:   or a theorem believed true from memory is insufficient.
37: - Identify the baseline revision/old paragraph IDs separately from the current
38:   new producer. A new N's origin label must state the historical/current
39:   distinction; a bare old R number is ambiguous after consumer editing.
40: - The expected avoided repeated work. An occurrence count is not measured
41:   formalization cost and does not by itself establish a speed benefit.
42: - The scope at each occurrence, including bound variables, temporary
43:   assumptions, definition guards and local facts established before the span.
44: 
45: Prefer a statement already justified at the cuts. Do not generalize its domain,
46: change representations, weaken conditions or introduce new mathematics merely
47: to make more occurrences match. If the proposed derivation needs an earlier
48: local calculation, include that calculation with its justified inputs. Never
49: declare an unexported local fact to be an available graph input.
50: 
51: Temporary assumptions stay closed in an implication or other complete
52: proposition; they cannot become H roots. An extraction that moves a witness,
53: choice, definition or binder across a scope boundary needs an explicit account
54: of the values and properties used afterwards. If that account cannot be made
55: locally and clearly, leave the original argument in place.
56: 
57: ## 2. Write the patch boundary before editing
58: 
59: Prepare an edit allowlist for one candidate or one coherent batch:
60: 
61: | Part | Allowed edit |
62: | --- | --- |
63: | New shared theorem | One fresh N and its R producer, with a complete statement and derivation from existing permitted inputs. |
64: | Actual consumers | Replace only the located repeated proof spans by a complete application; adjust direct inputs, citations and application accounting accordingly. |
65: | Necessary local bookkeeping | Update the directly affected binder/reference accounting and generated views. Record every such edit explicitly. |
66: | Everything else | Preserve the existing record content; do not reorder or renumber it as a cleanup. |
67: 
68: Keep the entire frozen specification unchanged: target P, original H, parameter
69: domains, global definitions/notation, logic, pins and E/M source inventories and
70: statements. Preserve all existing N/P statements and every unmodified argument
71: span. New sources, changed hypotheses, new global definitions, removed existing
72: nodes, or a changed old output are outside this fast factoring operation.
73: 
74: Copy an existing derivation rather than writing a new proof route. The new
75: producer may use only its declared inputs, global definitions and legitimate
76: local derivations. It cannot depend on a consumer output or its descendants.
77: Do not split each consumer into additional source nodes around the shared fact.
78: 
79: Each consumer application must state the parameter substitution, which inputs
80: or local proved facts discharge each condition, and the exact conclusion used.
81: Remove a former direct input only if the remaining argument no longer uses it;
82: retain it when it still has a direct role. A shared theorem is never ambient.
83: 
84: If an edit escapes the allowlist, return that candidate to the shortlist or
85: leave it unextracted. A source defect goes through the existing gap procedure;
86: do not turn a reuse optimization into a repair or a new research route.
87: 
88: ## 3. Check structural preservation globally, reasoning locally
89: 
90: Compare canonical JSON records by stable IDs, not only rendered text or changed
91: line numbers. Record before/after hashes and the actual changed fields/spans.
92: Reject any unexplained diff. Check these global mechanical invariants:
93: 
94: - The frozen specification and protected records are unchanged.
95: - All IDs/references resolve; definitions and guards remain available; there
96:   is no cycle or unsupported initial node; every N/P still has one producer.
97: - Every retained node remains in P's dependency closure. Reject the candidate
98:   if it would require deleting or reorganizing unrelated nodes to restore this.
99: - All consumers declare their actual inputs and remain self-contained. Only
100:   the explicit allowlisted nodes/fields have changed.
101: 
102: Run the existing `../scripts/nl0.py check` on the revised graph and specification.
103: Rechecking graph metadata across the package is allowed and inexpensive relative
104: to rereading every mathematical proof. It does not require a new LLM proof of
105: every node, and it does not establish the semantics of a substitution.
106: 
107: Distinguish **review impact** from **dependency status**. The new producer and
108: edited application boundaries need new mathematical review. An unchanged
109: downstream proof whose input statements and conventions are unchanged need not
110: be reconstructed merely because its ancestors have a new producer. Its final
111: acceptance nevertheless depends on the replacement producer being accepted.
112: Until that happens, affected descendants are pending, not newly accepted.
113: 
114: ## 4. Incremental Audit A: review the new proof and the substitution cuts
115: 
116: This is an incremental review procedure under Audit A's mathematical
117: obligations, not permission to weaken source verification or invent a fresh
118: packet replay. The version-bound receipt limitation below is part of the rule.
119: 
120: First inspect the baseline audit and its evidence bindings. Reuse a judgment
121: only for the exact previously reviewed content, context and evidence. Carry
122: FAIL, UNVERIFIED, inaccessible sources and disclosure limits forward. A source
123: file hash proves byte identity, not that an auditor ever inspected the theorem.
124: An unaudited baseline cannot acquire whole-proof acceptance through extraction.
125: 
126: Review the **new N/R in full**: complete statement, exact inputs, argument,
127: dependency accounting, scopes, guards and E/M applications, and the normal
128: fresh packet-only replay requirement. The extracted proof may be copied, but
129: its new closed interface and context must actually be checked.
130: 
131: For **each changed consumer**, review a substitution cut rather than rewriting
132: or replaying its entire old proof by default:
133: 
134: 1. Compare the old derived conclusion at the cut with the instantiated shared
135:    result, including all conditions, quantifiers and semantic conventions.
136: 2. Check that every condition of the shared theorem follows from that consumer's
137:    declared inputs or explicit in-scope local derivations, without extra facts.
138: 3. Check the interface to the untouched continuation: every subsequently used
139:    proposition, object, value and scope remains available with the same meaning.
140:    Equal output text alone cannot establish preservation of a selected witness.
141: 4. Verify the changed direct-input/citation/application accounting. Reuse source
142:    identity evidence only when unchanged; check every new source application.
143: 5. Bind the untouched remainder to its old reviewed bytes and old review
144:    evidence. Record exactly which old checks are inherited and which new checks
145:    cover the patch. Do not relabel this comparison as a new fresh whole-R replay.
146: 
147: If those boundaries do not justify inheritance, mark that candidate
148: `DEFERRED_NOT_LOCAL` and keep the baseline argument. Do not automatically expand
149: to a full-case audit. A separately requested broader review may inspect the
150: specific unresolved node, but is not part of this fast extraction.
151: 
152: Unchanged target/source/definition reviews and proof regions need no new
153: mathematical re-review when their audited content, applicable context and
154: evidence are unchanged. Do not reopen source searches solely because a global
155: graph hash changed. Changes or failures in their evidence invalidate reuse.
156: 
157: The result is a chain: baseline audit + exact revision + actual new reviews.
158: It is not a copied PASS with an updated graph hash. Record actual reviewer
159: exposure; old-review access is appropriate for delta review and cannot be called
160: an independent fresh packet-only review. This procedure authorizes no additional
161: agent or external-service dispatch.
162: 
163: ## 5. Seal or leave the candidate unextracted
164: 
165: Seal only after the allowlist/diff and graph checks pass and the scoped
166: mathematical review is complete. Keep original and revised manifests, patch,
167: location map, old/new evidence, pending findings and measured preparation cost.
168: Stage all candidate edits transactionally; a failed candidate must not replace
169: the accepted baseline. Do not launch formalization workers for an unaccepted
170: source revision or reuse task packets bound to the old graph.
171: 
172: Then finalize and freeze typed interfaces, shared Lean ports and local plans;
173: only afterwards generate worker packets. Shared Lean interface discovery may
174: use this preparation pass, but must not silently mutate the sealed NL0 later.
175: No extraction is a valid outcome; do not manufacture shared lemmas to satisfy
176: the workflow. The work is bounded by the chosen proof regions and patch size,
177: not a universal minute count. Longer time alone is not a mathematical gap.
178: 
179: ## Executable acceptance and review responsibilities
180: 
181: The unchanged parent checker still binds ordinary audit v3 to the complete
182: graph. `scripts/source_preparation.py` adds a separate incremental record;
183: it never copies old PASS fields into a forged fresh whole-graph audit.
184: Audit B and `workflow.py` both revalidate that record and all underlying evidence.
185: See [commands and the patch contract](integrated-workflow.md).
186: 
187: The initial executable scope is current-v2 source and nonoverlapping consumer
188: paragraph substitutions. Old proposition records/specification, unlisted R
189: records, untouched paragraphs and local fact/assumption lifetimes are protected.
190: Consumer source-application changes can remove obsolete uses, not introduce new
191: external uses. A broader refactor is deferred rather than widening this operation.
192: Multiple proposed edits to one consumer must first be merged into one coherent
193: candidate or left unextracted. Legacy test copies remain development evidence.
194: 
195: Separate three responsibilities:
196: 
197: - A producer reviewer sees only the complete new per-R packet and audits its
198:   conditional mathematics under ordinary Audit A, including actual fresh replay.
199:   Do not ask that packet to establish whole-graph acceptance or old-copy provenance.
200: - A substitution reviewer sees paired before/after consumers, the proposed shared
201:   statement, original derivations and explicit cut contract. `old_derivation`
202:   names THIS consumer's replaced proof; `producer_source_derivation` names the
203:   one original proof used to export the shared lemma. Its supplier may be a
204:   different consumer with a different final goal. Compare the common intermediate
205:   conclusion, not equality of those final goals. Check existing-proof
206:   factoring, each condition, exact supplied conclusion, continuation and accounting.
207:   This is delta review with baseline access, not fresh whole-consumer replay.
208: - Python checks canonical fanout, edit scope, graph validity, immutable evidence,
209:   the exact coverage partition and inherited acceptance/qualifications. It does
210:   not judge natural-language mathematics or authenticate a dishonest reviewer.
211: 
212: Internal N applications are direct inputs, paragraph citations and explicit prose;
213: the parent's `applications` source records remain E/M-only. Do not invent an N
214: source-application record to satisfy a reviewer. A prose citation without a real
215: substitution is not successful factoring. Derivation labels and fanout guesses
216: from a model are leads, not canonical graph facts.
217: 
218: Each cut review binds the exact supplied packet hash. Retain the binding from
219: the generated template and verify it during acceptance. Reusing an actual old
220: review after a record-only change requires identical canonical mathematics and
221: byte-identical actual reviewed packets; preserve its verdicts, notes, evidence
222: and original cost, and disclose that no new mathematical review occurred.
223: 
224: `INCREMENTAL-AUDIT-A-PASSED` requires a passing current baseline plus all actual
225: new producer/cut reviews. Missing/failed baseline checks remain inherited and
226: yield development-only local review. Every later consumer acceptance still
227: depends on the new producer; unchanged input statements and context permit
228: inheriting the old conditional argument without rereading it mathematically.
229: No fixed completion-time threshold makes a candidate worthwhile or incorrect.
